hero.intro: I build practical tools and solve problems for education, businesses and community by turning messy, manual processes into automated systems to make people's life easier.

about.heading: A builder with an eye for impact.
about.intro: I turn manual, messy processes into clear tools — usually with a spreadsheet, a sensor, or a little code.
paragraphs: I'm a student developer with a strong foundation in coding, mathematics and technology integration. I specialise in creating impactful educational tools, and I have experience developing solutions that improve learning for both teachers and students.

Most of my work starts with a real person and a frustrating, manual process — a teacher compiling reports by hand, a driver unsure how far they travelled, or a logistics team tracking hundreds of schools in a spreadsheet. I like taking that mess and turning it into something clear, reliable and genuinely useful.

work.heading: Tools built for real people.
work.intro: Eleven projects across apps, web, hardware and AI. Each one started with a specific problem — and was built to make someone's day a little lighter.

projects.title: AI Logistics Agent
projects.summary: An AI assistant inside Google Sheets that answers questions about a 204-school tablet rollout — deadlines, overdue tasks and contacts — without scanning thousands of rows.
projects.timelineNote: An AI assistant embedded in Google Sheets for a 204-school tablet rollout.

paragraphs: All over Sarawak, many schools don't have opportunities for students to catch up in their studies. Some students can't even read or write. There are many people involved in helping them: teachers, delivery drivers and volunteers.

The problems start before the tablets are even delivered. The devices are loaded with educational material from the Kayam App, but managing a 204-school logistics rollout is complex — and the people involved have no easy way to see what is overdue or what is coming next.
How can we make it easy for everyone involved to know what is overdue and what the upcoming deadlines are?

bullets.title: Students left behind
bullets.text: Many schools in Sarawak lack opportunities for students to catch up; some can't even read or write.

bullets.title: Logistics complexity
bullets.text: Teachers, delivery drivers and volunteers all need to coordinate across 204 schools.

bullets.title: Deadline visibility
bullets.text: There was no easy way to know which tasks were overdue or which deadlines were approaching.

bullets.title: Data overload
bullets.text: Over 1,000 rows of tracking data made manual lookups slow and error-prone.

paragraphs: Mr Chong, my teacher at Chumbaka, suggested developing an AI agent inside Google Sheets that could answer questions based on what users ask. The agent works like a human assistant — except it has everything stored in the database.

I connected ChatGPT to Google Sheets with Google Apps Script, then solved the scaling problem by adding a vector database. Instead of re-reading a thousand-page book every time, the agent flips straight to the paragraph it needs.

cards.title: The tool: Google Sheets
cards.text: Used Google Sheets because of prior experience, leveraging Google Apps Script and Python to build the solution.

cards.title: The initial challenge
cards.text: At the start, I wasn't even sure it would work. Eventually I connected ChatGPT to Google Sheets and coded it to respond to simple questions before reading sheet data.

cards.title: Scaling to 1,000+ rows
cards.text: Getting the AI to read all the data was like giving someone a 1,000-page book and asking one question. It was too slow and too costly to repeat every time.

cards.title: The vector database
cards.text: The AI now uses a smart index to find the exact passage instantly. Data syncs to the cloud manually or every one to two hours.

paragraphs: The final product lets anyone using the sheet get their question answered immediately, without slowly searching across rows of content. It turns a data-heavy spreadsheet into a conversation.

projects.title: Kayam Tracking App
projects.summary: A Python registration tool that tracks hundreds of government tablets on their way to schools in Sarawak — in real time.
projects.timelineNote: A real-time tracking tool for government tablets sent to Sarawak schools.

paragraphs: In many schools in Sarawak, there are students who are already ten years old but still can't speak or read. To help them, the government decided to send hundreds of tablets to Sarawak.

These tablets have the Kayam App, which helps students who are trailing to catch up to the level they're supposed to be at. However, it was very difficult to track the delivery of the tablets since people used to do it manually.

I developed a Python-based registration tool integrated with the Google Sheets API so that I could get real-time data. The system automatically logs, verifies and monitors the tablets that are distributed.
This made sure that every part of the process was automated, with no mistakes or missing data, making it much easier and faster to track all the tablets sent to schools.

projects.title: Map Mileage Calculator
projects.summary: A web tool that calculates delivery distances and driver earnings automatically — with proof of the kilometres actually driven.
projects.timelineNote: A web tool that calculates delivery distances and driver earnings.

paragraphs: In addition to the Kayam Tracking App, the drivers who delivered the tablets didn't know how much they would earn for each trip. There was also a risk that some drivers might cheat about the number of kilometres they had driven to get more money.

I built a web-based tool that uses mapping data to automatically calculate the distance and total mileage between locations. It then calculates the driver's earnings based on the number of kilometres covered.
This helps provide proof of the actual distance driven and ensures that each driver gets paid the correct amount based on accurate data.

projects.title: Chumbaka Student Report Tool
projects.summary: An AppSheet system that lets teachers submit student projects digitally and generates personalised PDF reports at the end of each term.
projects.timelineNote: A digital project showcase and report generator for Chumbaka teachers.

paragraphs: Chumbaka didn't have a proper system to analyse and showcase the good projects that students had completed. Everything had to be done manually, which took a lot of time and effort.

I created an AppSheet-based system integrated with Google Sheets. Teachers can submit student projects through a digital form that includes photos and descriptions. The tool then automatically compiles and generates personalised reports for each student.
At the end of each term, a PDF report is automatically generated to show each student's progress and achievements, making it easier for teachers to highlight outstanding projects.

projects.title: Interactive Chemistry Platform
projects.summary: A free, visual chemistry learning website that turns abstract textbook concepts into interactive lessons and simulations.
projects.timelineNote: A free, interactive website that makes chemistry visible.

paragraphs: Students found chemistry abstract and difficult to understand through traditional textbook learning.
Built a free, interactive website offering visual lessons and engaging simulations that make chemistry concepts accessible to all learners.
Empowered students to enjoy learning chemistry, increasing engagement and comprehension through interactive and visual resources.

projects.title: Alpha Course Analysis Tool
projects.summary: A one-click Google Sheets analysis tool that gave the HTBB team clear insight into 11 years of Alpha Course participants.
projects.timelineNote: A one-click analysis tool for 11 years of Alpha Course data.

paragraphs: After 11 years of running the Alpha Course, the organisers still didn't have clear information about the participants, such as their age, church attendance or reasons for joining. All the data was there, but it wasn't analysed in a useful way.

I developed an automated analysis tool in Google Sheets that processes all the participant data with just one click. It organises information such as age, church attendance and reasons for attending, making it easy to understand the overall trends.
This helped the HTBB team quickly gain clear insights into their participants, allowing them to improve outreach strategies and plan future Alpha sessions more effectively.

projects.title: Young Innovators Judging System
projects.summary: A real-time AppSheet judging form that replaced paper score sheets for the national finals of the Young Innovators Challenge.
projects.timelineNote: A digital judging system used at the 2025 national finals.

paragraphs: Judges in the Young Innovators Challenge had to evaluate projects using paper forms, which made it difficult to update or change scores based on students' performance. The process was slow and not very flexible.

I developed an AppSheet-based form that allows judges to submit, edit and manage scores easily in real time. The interface is simple and seamless, helping judges focus on the evaluation rather than the paperwork.
This digital judging system was used for the national finals of the Young Innovators Challenge in 2025, making the entire judging process faster, more accurate and more efficient.

projects.title: Vaccine Temperature Monitor
projects.summary: An Arduino monitoring system that protects COVID-19 vaccines from spoilage with real-time temperature alerts.
projects.timelineNote: An Arduino system to prevent COVID-19 vaccine spoilage.

paragraphs: Vaccines were at risk of spoilage due to undetected temperature fluctuations during storage.
Created an Arduino-based temperature monitoring system with real-time LED and sound alerts to detect deviations from the safe temperature range.
Prevented potential vaccine spoilage and ensured safe distribution during the pandemic, contributing to reliable healthcare logistics.

projects.title: Being Present Together
projects.summary: A family engagement app built with MIT App Inventor to help households have more meaningful time together.
projects.timelineNote: An app that helps families put down their phones and reconnect.

paragraphs: Families struggled to have meaningful conversations and spend quality time together in the digital age.
Developed an app using MIT App Inventor and design thinking principles, featuring conversation prompts, activity scheduling and interactive engagement features.
Encouraged families to reconnect, improving communication and emotional bonds through structured, intentional activities.

projects.title: Wake Up Ah Kong
projects.summary: An Arduino assistive device that helps my grandfather get out of bed safely using distance sensors and gentle alerts.
projects.timelineNote: An Arduino assistive device built for my grandfather.

paragraphs: My grandfather faced difficulty waking up safely due to mobility and balance issues.
Designed an Arduino-based assistive device using ultrasonic sensors, sound alerts and visual indicators to detect when he approaches the bed edge.
Improved safety and independence for the elderly, providing peace of mind to family members through proactive alert systems.

projects.title: Spinning Star Alarm Clock
projects.summary: A playful alarm clock that plays music, flashes LEDs and spins a star — because waking up should be fun.
projects.timelineNote: A playful alarm clock with music, light and a spinning star.

paragraphs: Conventional alarm clocks fail to make waking up enjoyable or motivating, especially for children.
Designed a creative alarm clock that plays "Mary Had a Little Lamb", lights up with blinking LEDs and spins a star when the alarm triggers.
Transformed waking up into a fun and engaging experience, combining creativity, music and technology in everyday life.
